name: Pharma & life sciences
tagline: Pharmacy sales and margin, batch expiry, medical-rep calls and coverage, prescriptions and clinical-trial safety
description: Item-wise sales and batch-wise stock registers from pharmacy billing software (Marg ERP, GoFrugal, RetailGraph and Medeil in India; PioneerRx and McKesson pharmacy systems elsewhere) with batch, expiry, MRP, PTR and drug schedule; medical-representative daily call reports (DCR) from field-force CRMs such as Veeva CRM, IQVIA OCE and Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud; prescriber-level prescription data (TRx and NRx); and clinical-trial datasets in CDISC SDTM and ADaM style (DM, AE, ADSL, ADAE with USUBJID, AETERM, AESEV, AESER) exported from EDC systems such as Medidata Rave or Veeva Vault EDC, plus safety case listings.

fields.label: Bill / invoice number
fields.description: Identifies each bill; repeats on every item line of the bill.

fields.label: Medicine / product
fields.description: The brand or item sold, stocked, detailed on a call or reported in an adverse event.

fields.label: Expiry (as written)
fields.description: An expiry kept as text (08/26, Aug-26) rather than a date: usable as a label, not for expiry calculations.

fields.label: Pack
fields.description: The pack the item is sold in (10 TAB, 100 ML, 1 VIAL).

fields.label: GST / tax amount
fields.description: Tax on the bill line; kept for reference, since CGST and SGST often sit in separate columns.

fields.label: Purchase rate / PTR
fields.description: What the pharmacy paid per unit (purchase rate or price to retailer), used for margin.

fields.label: Sales amount
fields.description: Value of the bill line after line discount.

fields.label: Month / period
fields.description: A month or period column, as in prescription audits and monthly field-force summaries.

fields.label: POB value
fields.description: Personal order booking: an order a chemist or stockist places during the call.

subDomains.name: Pharmacy sales & dispensing
subDomains.description: One row per bill line (an item and batch sold) from a pharmacy's billing software, with quantity, MRP, rate, amount and often the prescribing doctor and drug schedule.

subDomains.name: Field-force calls & prescriptions
subDomains.description: One row per call a medical representative made on a doctor, chemist or stockist (daily call report), or per prescriber per month with prescription counts (TRx, NRx).

subDomains.name: Batch stock & expiry
subDomains.description: One row per item batch held in stock, with its expiry, quantity and value, as in a batch-wise stock or near-expiry statement.

subDomains.name: Clinical-trial subjects & adverse events
subDomains.description: One row per adverse event (SDTM AE or ADaM ADAE) or per trial subject (DM or ADSL), with subject, site, arm, severity, seriousness and outcome.

kpis.name: Net sales
kpis.definition: Value of medicines and other items sold in the period, after line discounts.
kpis.formula: Σ sales amount

variants.label: Quantity × selling rate
variants.caveat: No sales amount column, so sales are quantity × selling rate, before any bill-level discount.

variants.label: Quantity × MRP
variants.caveat: No sales amount or selling rate, so sales are valued at MRP, which overstates what was collected when discounts are given.

pitfalls: Sales returns entered as negative lines lower the total; registers that keep returns in a separate file must be netted before comparing periods.

kpis.name: Bills
kpis.definition: Distinct bills (customer transactions) raised in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct bill numbers

variants.label: Row count (no bill number)
variants.caveat: No bill number, so every row is counted as one bill; in an item-wise register this counts lines, not bills.

kpis.name: Average bill value
kpis.definition: Average value of one bill.
kpis.formula: Net sales ÷ distinct bills
pitfalls: Bulk bills from clinics and nursing homes raise the average; look at them separately.

kpis.name: Gross margin %
kpis.definition: Share of sales value left after the purchase cost of the units sold.
kpis.formula: (Σ sales amount − Σ quantity × purchase rate) ÷ Σ sales amount, on lines that have all three

variants.label: Quantity × (selling rate − purchase rate)
variants.caveat: No sales amount column, so margin is measured on quantity × selling rate, before bill-level discounts.

variants.label: Quantity × (MRP − purchase rate)
variants.caveat: No sales amount or selling rate, so this is the margin at MRP: the most the pharmacy could earn before any discount at the counter.

pitfalls: Free (scheme) units cost nothing, so a margin on billed quantity alone understates the real margin when schemes are large.
The purchase rate must be per the same unit as the quantity sold (per strip, not per box).

kpis.name: Units sold
kpis.definition: Units (strips, bottles, packs) billed in the period, excluding free scheme units.
kpis.formula: Σ quantity
pitfalls: Units mix strips, bottles and loose tablets; compare units only within one product.

kpis.name: Prescription-only share of sales
kpis.definition: Share of sales value from prescription-only (scheduled) medicines, among lines whose schedule is recorded.
kpis.formula: Sales of Rx (scheduled) lines ÷ sales of lines with a schedule

variants.label: Rx sales ÷ sales with a schedule
Rx lines ÷ lines with a schedule
variants.caveat: No sales amount, so the share is measured by number of bill lines.

pitfalls: Schedules differ by country (Schedule H, H1 and X in India; POM, P and GSL in the UK; DEA schedules in the US): check how your software codes them.

kpis.name: Calls reported
kpis.definition: Calls (visits to doctors, chemists or stockists) reported by representatives in the period, met or not.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct call IDs

variants.label: Rows with a call date
variants.caveat: No call ID, so every row with a call date is one call.

variants.label: Rows with a call status
variants.caveat: No call ID or call date, so every row with a call status is one call.

variants.label: Rows with a representative
variants.caveat: No call ID, call date or status, so every row with a representative is one call.

kpis.name: Doctors met
kpis.definition: Distinct doctors (or other customers) met at least once in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct doctors with a met call

variants.label: Distinct doctor names, met calls
variants.caveat: No doctor code, so doctors are counted by name: namesakes merge and spelling variants split.

variants.label: Distinct doctor codes, any call
variants.caveat: No call status, so every doctor with a reported call counts as met.

variants.label: Distinct doctor names, any call
variants.caveat: No doctor code or call status: doctors with a reported call, counted by name.

kpis.name: Doctor coverage
kpis.definition: Share of the doctors listed in the file (met, missed or planned) who were met at least once in the period.
kpis.formula: Doctors met ÷ doctors in the file

variants.label: Doctor codes met ÷ doctor codes listed
Doctor names met ÷ doctor names listed
variants.caveat: No doctor code, so doctors are matched by name.

pitfalls: A call file lists only doctors someone planned or visited; doctors on the master list (MCL) who were never planned are missing, so coverage looks higher than it is against the full list.

kpis.name: Call average
kpis.definition: Calls met per representative per day in the field.
kpis.formula: Met calls ÷ rep-days (each representative's distinct reporting dates, added up)

variants.label: Calls ÷ rep-days
variants.caveat: No call status, so every reported call counts, met or not.

variants.label: Met calls ÷ rep-days (main date column)
variants.caveat: No call-date column, so the main date column is taken as the call date.

variants.label: Calls ÷ rep-days (main date column)
variants.caveat: No call-date column or call status: the main date column is taken as the call date and every reported call counts.

pitfalls: Call dates that carry a time of day split one working day into several; use a date-only call date.
Only days with at least one reported call count as field days, so days with nothing reported are invisible.

kpis.name: Samples given
kpis.definition: Units of free physician samples handed out on calls in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ samples given

kpis.name: Total prescriptions (TRx)
kpis.definition: Prescriptions written in the period, new and refills.
kpis.formula: Σ TRx
pitfalls: Prescription audits are projected from a sample of pharmacies; compare trends within one data source, not absolute counts across sources.

kpis.name: Stock value
kpis.definition: Value of stock held on the latest stock date in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ stock value on the latest as-on date (semi-additive)

variants.label: Stock value, single snapshot
variants.caveat: No as-on date, so the file is treated as one point-in-time stock statement.

variants.label: Quantity × purchase rate, latest stock date
variants.caveat: No stock value column, so stock is valued at quantity × purchase rate.

variants.label: Quantity × purchase rate, single snapshot
variants.caveat: No stock value or as-on date: stock is valued at quantity × purchase rate and the file is treated as one snapshot.

pitfalls: Stock is semi-additive: add across items and stores on one date, never across dates.

kpis.name: Units in stock
kpis.definition: Units held on the latest stock date in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ stock quantity on the latest as-on date (semi-additive)

variants.label: Single snapshot
variants.caveat: No as-on date, so the file is treated as one point-in-time stock statement.

kpis.name: Batches in stock
kpis.definition: Item batches holding stock on the latest stock date (one per row of a batch-wise stock statement).
kpis.formula: Rows with stock quantity above zero, latest as-on date

variants.label: Batch lines with stock, latest stock date
Batch lines with stock, single snapshot
variants.caveat: No as-on date, so the file is treated as one stock statement.

variants.label: Distinct batch numbers
variants.caveat: No stock quantity, so every distinct batch number counts; a batch code shared by two products counts once.

kpis.name: Expired stock share
kpis.definition: Share of stock value in batches already past expiry on the stock date.
kpis.formula: Stock value with expiry before the as-on date ÷ stock value with an expiry, latest as-on date

variants.label: By value, expiry before the stock date
By value, days to expiry ≤ 0
variants.caveat: Uses the days-to-expiry column; with several stock dates in the file, every date's stock is pooled.

variants.label: By units, expiry before the stock date
variants.caveat: No stock value, so the share is measured in units.

variants.label: By units, days to expiry ≤ 0
variants.caveat: No stock value, so the share is measured in units from the days-to-expiry column.

pitfalls: An expiry written as month and year (03/26) is read as the first of that month, so a batch counts as expired from the start of its expiry month although it may be sold until the month ends.
Expired stock awaiting return to the supplier stays in this share until it leaves the stock statement.

kpis.name: Near-expiry stock share
kpis.definition: Share of stock value in batches that expire within the next 90 days (not yet expired).
kpis.formula: Stock value with 1–90 days to expiry ÷ stock value with a days-to-expiry value

variants.label: By units, 1–90 days to expiry
variants.caveat: No stock value, so the share is measured in units.

pitfalls: Needs a days-to-expiry column: Loupe never assumes today's date. Many suppliers accept expiry returns only within a set window, so act on this list before batches expire.

kpis.name: Average remaining shelf life
kpis.definition: Average days from the stock date to expiry across batch lines in stock.
kpis.formula: Average of (expiry date − as-on date) over batch lines with stock, latest as-on date

variants.label: Expiry − stock date, lines with stock
Days-to-expiry column, lines with stock
variants.caveat: Uses the days-to-expiry column.

variants.label: Expiry − stock date, every line
variants.caveat: No stock quantity, so every batch line counts, including empty ones.

variants.label: Days-to-expiry column, every line
variants.caveat: No stock quantity, so every batch line counts, including empty ones.

pitfalls: A simple average over batch lines: a large slow-moving batch and a small one weigh the same.

kpis.name: Subjects
kpis.definition: Distinct trial subjects in the file and period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct subject IDs (USUBJID)
pitfalls: An adverse-event listing holds only subjects who had an event; the number of subjects exposed comes from the subject list (DM or ADSL).

kpis.name: Adverse events
kpis.definition: Adverse events recorded in the period (one per row with an event term).
kpis.formula: Count of rows with an adverse-event term
pitfalls: Counts events, not subjects: one subject with many events weighs as much as many subjects with one each.

kpis.name: Serious AE share
kpis.definition: Share of adverse events that were serious (death, life-threatening, hospitalisation, disability, congenital anomaly or another important medical event).
kpis.formula: Serious AEs ÷ AEs with a seriousness flag

kpis.name: Severe AE share
kpis.definition: Share of adverse events rated severe, or CTCAE grade 3 or higher.
kpis.formula: Severe (grade ≥ 3) AEs ÷ AEs with a severity
pitfalls: Severity (mild, moderate, severe) and seriousness are different things: a severe headache is rarely a serious AE.

kpis.name: Drug-related AE share
kpis.definition: Share of adverse events the investigator judged related to the study drug.
kpis.formula: Related AEs ÷ AEs with a causality assessment
pitfalls: Causality scales differ (related/not related, or a five-point scale from certain to unlikely); check which answers your file counts as related.

kpis.name: AEs leading to drug withdrawal
kpis.definition: Share of adverse events after which the study drug was permanently withdrawn.
kpis.formula: AEs with action taken = drug withdrawn ÷ AEs with an action recorded

variants.label: Drug withdrawn ÷ events with an action

kpis.name: Prescriptions dispensed
kpis.definition: Distinct prescriptions filled in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct prescription numbers

kpis.name: Items per bill
kpis.definition: Average number of item lines on a bill.
kpis.formula: Bill lines with an item ÷ distinct bills

kpis.name: Gross margin value
kpis.definition: Sales value left after the purchase cost of the units sold.
kpis.formula: Σ sales amount − Σ quantity × purchase rate, on lines that have all three

variants.label: Quantity × (selling rate − purchase rate)
variants.caveat: No sales amount column, so margin is measured on quantity × selling rate, before bill-level discounts.

kpis.name: Counter discount rate
kpis.definition: Discount given as a share of sales before discount.
kpis.formula: Σ discount ÷ (Σ sales amount + Σ discount), on lines with both

variants.label: Discount ÷ sales at MRP
variants.caveat: No sales amount, so the discount is compared with sales at MRP.

pitfalls: Software differs on whether the amount column is before or after discount; check one bill by hand.

kpis.name: Free-goods share
kpis.definition: Free (scheme or bonus) units as a share of all units moved.
kpis.formula: Σ free quantity ÷ (Σ quantity + Σ free quantity)

kpis.name: Customers served
kpis.definition: Distinct patients or customers billed in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct patients or customers
pitfalls: Walk-in sales are often billed to one generic name (Cash, Walk-in), which counts as a single customer.

kpis.name: Repeat customer share
kpis.definition: Share of customers billed on two or more bills in the period.
kpis.formula: Customers with ≥ 2 bills ÷ customers served

variants.label: Customers with 2+ rows ÷ customers
variants.caveat: No bill number, so every row counts as a visit; a bill with two items makes a repeat customer.

kpis.name: Prescribing doctors
kpis.definition: Distinct doctors whose prescriptions were filled in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct doctors on bills

kpis.name: Met call rate
kpis.definition: Share of reported calls where the doctor or customer was actually met.
kpis.formula: Met calls ÷ calls with a status

kpis.name: Representatives reporting
kpis.definition: Distinct representatives who reported at least one call in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct representatives

kpis.name: Calls per doctor
kpis.definition: Average number of met calls on each doctor met in the period.
kpis.formula: Met calls ÷ doctors met

variants.label: Calls ÷ doctors called on
variants.caveat: No call status, so every reported call counts.

pitfalls: Companies set a visit frequency per doctor category (for example two or three calls a month on core doctors); compare by category, not overall.

kpis.name: New prescriptions (NRx)
kpis.definition: New prescriptions written in the period (not refills).
kpis.formula: Σ NRx

kpis.name: NRx share of TRx
kpis.definition: Share of all prescriptions that are new rather than refills, a lead indicator of growth.
kpis.formula: Σ NRx ÷ Σ TRx, on rows with both

kpis.name: Prescribers writing
kpis.definition: Distinct prescribers who wrote at least one prescription in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct prescribers with TRx above zero

variants.label: Distinct prescriber names with TRx > 0
variants.caveat: No prescriber code, so prescribers are counted by name.

kpis.name: Orders booked (POB)
kpis.definition: Value of orders chemists and stockists placed during calls.
kpis.formula: Σ POB value

kpis.name: Joint-work share
kpis.definition: Share of calls made together with a manager.
kpis.formula: Calls with joint work ÷ calls with the flag recorded

kpis.name: Expired stock value
kpis.definition: Value of stock in batches already past expiry on the stock date.
kpis.formula: Σ stock value with expiry before the as-on date, latest as-on date

variants.label: Days to expiry ≤ 0
variants.caveat: Uses the days-to-expiry column; with several stock dates in the file, every date's stock is added.

kpis.name: Near-expiry stock value
kpis.definition: Value of stock in batches that expire within the next 90 days (not yet expired).
kpis.formula: Σ stock value with 1–90 days to expiry

variants.label: 1–90 days to expiry, latest stock date
1–90 days to expiry, single snapshot
variants.caveat: No as-on date, so the file is treated as one stock statement.

kpis.name: Items in stock
kpis.definition: Distinct items with stock on hand on the latest stock date.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct items with stock quantity above zero, latest as-on date

variants.label: Single snapshot
variants.caveat: No as-on date, so the file is treated as one stock statement.

kpis.name: Subjects with an AE
kpis.definition: Distinct subjects with at least one adverse event in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct subjects with an AE term

kpis.name: AEs per affected subject
kpis.definition: Average number of adverse events among subjects who had at least one.
kpis.formula: Adverse events ÷ subjects with an AE

kpis.name: Subjects with a serious AE
kpis.definition: Distinct subjects with at least one serious adverse event.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct subjects with a serious AE

variants.label: Distinct subjects with a serious AE

kpis.name: Fatal AEs
kpis.definition: Adverse events whose outcome was death.
kpis.formula: Count of AEs with outcome = fatal

kpis.name: Study sites
kpis.definition: Distinct study sites in the file and period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct sites

kpis.name: Safety population
kpis.definition: Distinct subjects flagged as in the safety population (dosed at least once).
kpis.formula: Count of distinct subjects with the safety-population flag

kpis.name: Subjects per site
kpis.definition: Average number of subjects per study site.
kpis.formula: Subjects ÷ study sites

kpis.name: Subject discontinuation rate
kpis.definition: Share of randomised subjects who left the study early, for any reason.
kpis.formula: Subjects discontinued ÷ subjects with a disposition (screen failures excluded)
pitfalls: Subjects still on study are in the denominator, so the rate rises as the study runs.

kpis.name: Study completion rate
kpis.definition: Share of randomised subjects who completed the study.
kpis.formula: Subjects completed ÷ subjects with a disposition (screen failures excluded)

kpis.name: Screen failure rate
kpis.definition: Share of screened subjects who did not qualify for randomisation.
kpis.formula: Screen failures ÷ subjects with a disposition

variants.label: Screen failures ÷ subjects with a disposition

pitfalls: Many subject files hold only randomised subjects; screen failures then never appear and the rate reads zero.

kpis.name: Average AE duration
kpis.definition: Average days from onset to resolution, for adverse events with both dates.
kpis.formula: Average of (AE end date − AE start date)
pitfalls: Ongoing events have no end date and are left out, so long-running events are under-represented.

kpis.name: Samples per call
kpis.definition: Sample units handed out per reported call.
kpis.formula: Samples given ÷ calls reported

kpis.name: TRx per prescriber
kpis.definition: Prescriptions written per prescriber who wrote any.
kpis.formula: TRx ÷ prescribers writing

kpis.name: Mean age of subjects
kpis.definition: Average age of the subjects in the file, one value per subject.
kpis.formula: Average over subjects of their age

charts.title: Net sales over time
charts.reason: Sales per period are additive totals, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Average bill value
charts.reason: An average recomputed per period from its own bills, drawn as a line and never summed.

charts.title: Gross margin % over time
charts.reason: A ratio recomputed per period from sales and cost, so it reads as a line, never averaged across days.

charts.title: Top medicines by sales
charts.reason: One total compared across many named medicines: sorted horizontal bars keep long names readable. Top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Sales by manufacturer
charts.reason: Which companies' products sell: sorted bars per manufacturer, drilling into its medicines.

charts.title: Sales by therapeutic class
charts.reason: The therapy mix is a part-to-whole split across many classes, which a treemap shows with sizes that are easy to compare.

charts.title: Prescription and over-the-counter sales
charts.reason: A part-to-whole split across a handful of schedules: a donut of at most six slices shows it at a glance.

charts.title: Sales concentration by medicine (Pareto)
charts.reason: A few brands usually make most of a pharmacy's sales: columns per medicine with the cumulative share as a line on the same 0–100% axis show where stock and attention pay off.

charts.title: Gross margin % by manufacturer
charts.reason: A rate compared across companies: sorted bars of the recomputed margin, with manufacturers under 30 lines hidden as too small.

charts.title: Sales by prescribing doctor
charts.reason: Which doctors' prescriptions bring the most sales: sorted bars of the top 15.

charts.title: When customers buy
charts.reason: Two time dimensions and one count: a weekday × hour heatmap shows the counter's rush hours, for staffing.

charts.title: Medicine scorecard
charts.reason: Several measures per medicine side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Calls reported over time
charts.reason: Calls per period are discrete counts, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Call average over time
charts.reason: A ratio of calls to rep-days recomputed per period, so it is a line, never summed.

charts.title: Prescriptions (TRx) over time
charts.reason: Prescriptions per month are additive counts, so columns from zero compare them honestly.

charts.title: NRx share of TRx over time
charts.reason: A share recomputed each month from new and total prescriptions, drawn as a line.

charts.title: Calls by doctor speciality
charts.reason: Where the field force spends its calls: sorted bars per speciality, top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Calls met and missed
charts.reason: A part-to-whole split across a few call outcomes, which a donut shows at a glance.

charts.title: TRx by product
charts.reason: Prescription volume compared across brands: sorted horizontal bars, top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Doctor coverage by territory
charts.reason: A rate compared across territories: sorted bars of the recomputed coverage, with territories under 30 calls hidden.

charts.title: Call average by representative
charts.reason: Productivity compared across representatives: the recomputed call average per rep, sorted, with reps under 20 calls hidden.

charts.title: Samples given by product
charts.reason: Where sample budgets go: sorted bars per brand, to set against prescriptions.

charts.title: Prescription concentration by doctor (Pareto)
charts.reason: A small share of doctors usually writes most prescriptions: columns per doctor with the cumulative share on the same 0–100% axis show who to prioritise.

charts.title: Representative scorecard
charts.reason: Several measures per representative side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Stock value by expiry month
charts.reason: When today's stock expires: the stock value falling due in each month, as columns from zero, shows the batches to sell or return first.

charts.title: Stock value by manufacturer
charts.reason: Where money is tied up: a part-to-whole split of stock value across companies, drilling into their medicines.

charts.title: Stock value by store
charts.reason: Stock compared across stores or warehouses: sorted horizontal bars, top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Near-expiry share by manufacturer
charts.reason: Which companies' stock is ageing: the recomputed near-expiry share per manufacturer, sorted, with those under 20 batch lines hidden.

charts.title: Expired stock share by store
charts.reason: A rate compared across stores: the recomputed expired share, sorted, with stores under 20 batch lines hidden.

charts.title: Batches by days to expiry
charts.reason: Shelf life left is spread unevenly: a histogram of batch lines per band shows how much stock sits close to expiry.

charts.title: Stock by medicine
charts.reason: Several stock measures per medicine side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Adverse events by onset month
charts.reason: Events per period are discrete counts, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Serious AE share by onset month
charts.reason: A share recomputed per month from that month's events, drawn as a line and never averaged.

charts.title: Subjects enrolled over time
charts.reason: Enrolment per period as columns from zero shows the recruitment pace.

charts.title: Adverse events by body system
charts.reason: Events grouped by system organ class, as safety tables are, in sorted bars that drill into the terms.

charts.title: Most frequent adverse events
charts.reason: The commonest events by preferred term, sorted, as a safety summary lists them.

charts.title: Severity mix by treatment arm
charts.reason: Arms differ in size, so each arm's events are shown as 100% split by severity, which compares the mix rather than the counts.

charts.title: Serious AE share by treatment arm
charts.reason: A rate compared across a few arms: bars of the recomputed share, with arms under 20 events hidden.

charts.title: Drug-related AE share by treatment arm
charts.reason: Whether the study drug, rather than chance, drives events: the related share per arm, placebo beside active.

charts.title: Subjects by site
charts.reason: Recruitment compared across sites: sorted bars, top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Site safety scorecard
charts.reason: Several measures per site side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

pitfalls: Sales returns, expiry returns and free (scheme) units change both value and margin: net them before comparing medicines or periods.
Stock and expiry figures are snapshots: add them across items or stores on one date, never across dates.
Batch numbers are only unique within a product and manufacturer; identify a batch by product and batch together.
Call reports are self-reported: coverage and call average describe what was reported, and a file without missed or unplanned doctors overstates coverage.
Adverse-event shares here are crude event-level proportions, not incidence among exposed subjects; per-subject rates need the full subject list (DM or ADSL).
Small arms, sites, territories and medicines swing wildly; treat rates from fewer than about 30 rows as noise.
